lede: Health insurance claims management training helps claims professionals assess claims and distinguish suspicious activity from billing errors. It is for people in claims operations, fraud investigation, payment integrity, and compliance who need practical analytical and investigative skills. Participants practise adjudicating claims against policy terms and coding rules, profiling providers and interpreting anomaly flags, and structuring investigation case files and payment reviews.
audienceIntro: This course is built for mid-career professionals who work directly in health insurance claims operations, fraud investigation, payment integrity, or compliance — and who need to sharpen both their analytical and investigative capabilities.
modules: Clinical Coding Standards and Billing Compliance
Provider Risk Scoring and Utilization Profiling
AI-Assisted Anomaly Detection in Claims Data
Payment Integrity Reporting and Compliance Communication
prerequisites: Participants should have at least 1–2 years of working experience in health insurance claims processing, payment integrity, healthcare compliance, fraud investigation, or a closely related operational role. A working familiarity with basic claims adjudication concepts — including policy coverage terms, eligibility verification, and claims submission processes — is expected before attending. No programming, coding, or data science skills are required. AI-assisted fraud detection content is delivered at operational application level: you will learn to interpret and act on AI-generated outputs, not to build or configure the underlying models. Participants should bring a laptop capable of running Microsoft Excel or Power BI (free desktop version) for dashboard and scorecard exercises. All datasets, case materials, templates, and reference guides are provided by TrainingCred.
